text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.
WHEAT SALE - The CCC bought 4,410 tonnes U.S. SRW wheat for donation to Senegal at $168.50 a tonne for Oct 5-31 shipment.

WHEAT AND BARLEY SALE - The Japanese Food Agency said on Thursday it had bought 60,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat, 40,000 tonnes of Canadian wheat, 20,000 tonnes of Australian wheat and 80,000 tonnes of Australian barley at its weekly tender, all for November shipment.
CORN SALES - CCC buys 4,280 tonnes of U.S. no.2 yellow corn for donation to Angola at $142.98 a tonne for Oct 5-31.

- Taiwan's Members Feed Industry Group bought a 54,000-tonne shipment of U.S. No.2 corn from Mitsui at a spot tender. The corn was bought on a FOB basis at 63.74 cents/December CBOT contract for 36,000 tonnes and at $148.60 a tonne for 18,000 tonnes. Shipment was set for PNW Dec 6-20.
- South Korea's Korea Feed Association bought 52,000 tonnes of U.S. No.3 yellow corn at $158 per tonne C&F, traders said Arrival was set for February 15 at the western port city of Inchon.

VEGOIL SALE - El Salvador bought 3,800 tonnes tallow under the PL-480 export program for September 25-October 10 shipment, its U.S. export agent Panalpina Inc said. The tallow was acquired from Jacob Stern Co at $599.00 a tonne, FOB, out of the U.S. Gulf.
SOYA TENDER - Tunisia has launched a tender for Friday for the purchase of 13,000 tonnes or more of soy pellets for 25-October/5 November shipment, traders said.
BARLEY TENDER - Saudi Arabia will tender on September 20 to import a total of 1.72 million tonnes of optional-origin feed barley for delivery in October, November and December,
BARLEY TENDER - Turkey's state grain board said results of its tender to export barley would be announced on Friday.

The tender for at least 200,000 tonnes of feed and malting barley, attracted Tradigrain, Romak, Louis Dreyfus, Alfred Toepfer International, Glencore, Cargill International, Grains and Fourrages and BEM. FOB prices for feed barley ranged from $121 a tonne, by Tradigrain for 50,000 tonnes for November and December shipment, to $136.07 by Glencore for 125,000 tonnes for second half October. Feed barley shipment dates varied from October to end-December. FOB prices for malting barley were from $148 to $150.75.

WHEAT TENDERS - Pakistan will tender for 200,000 tonnes U.S.grade 2 or better soft white wheat under the export credit guarantee program (GSM-102) for October 10-31 shipment, its U.S. export agent said. Bids must be received on September 29 and will remain valid until Sepember 30.
- The CCC seeks up to 35,000 tonnes of U.S. No.2 or better soft red winter or soft white wheat for donation to Eritrea. Shipment is set for Oct 10-Nov 5. Offers are due by Sept 26.
- The CCC seeks up to 42,000 tonnes of U.S. No. 2 or better hard red winter wheat for donation to Georgia for Oct 10-Nov 5 shipment. Offers are due by September 23.

WHEAT TENDER - Syria's General Establishment for Cereal Processing and Trade offered 100,000 tonnes of hard amber durum wheat for sale for November shipment. October 1 was final date for offers. Confirmation is set on October 2.
- The CCC seeks 45,000 tonnes U.S. HRW wheat to donation for Ethiopia for November 1-25 and offers due by Sept 19.
CORN TENDER - Jordan is to seek 50,000 tonnes of U.S. Number 3 yellow corn for shipment in first half of November. Offers must be received by September 25.

CORN TENDER - The South African Maize Board was offering up to 33,000 tonnes of white corn for export in one unit of 20,000, 25,000 or 33,000 tonnes for shipment on October 23 to November 1, from Durban. The tender closes on September 25.
- CCC said it is seeking up to 16,000 tonnes U.S. No.2 or better yellow corn for donation to Rwanda. Shipment period is set for December 5-30 and offers are due by September 24.
RICE TENDER - The Republic of the Congo seeks to buy about 13,300 tonnes of U.S. long grain milled rice under PL-480 and offers are due by Wednesday. Shipment is for Nov 5-20.
SOYBEAN OIL TENDER - The Republic of the Congo seeks to buy 3,400 tonnes of PL-480 tonnes of soybean oil. Offers are due by Wednesday. Shipment is for November 5-20.

MARKET TALK - U.S. Senate Agriculture Committee Chairman Richard Lugar Thursday urged the U.S. Agriculture Department to resist pressure to renew commodity export subsidies under the Export Enhancement Program. In a letter to Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman, Lugar said renewed EEP would keep world prices artificially low compared with U.S. prices. It would encourage Canada to export wheat to the more lucrative U.S. market, Lugar said.
